chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-A'lawi (may Allah have mercy on him) told us, saying: My grandfather told me, saying: Ahmad ibn Salih al-Tamimi told me, saying: Abdullah ibn Isa told us, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both), saying:

Jibra'il (peace be upon him) gifted to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) the name of Hasan ibn Ali in a piece of silk from the clothes of Paradise, and he derived the name of al-Husayn from al-Hasan (peace be upon them both).
ai.seo_question: What is the origin and meaning of the names Hasan and Husayn according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to emphasize the divine etymology of the Imams' names, linking 'Husayn' directly to 'Hasan' to signify their shared spiritual essence and status. The gift of silk from Paradise by Jibra'il underscores the celestial origin of these names, reinforcing the Shia belief in the pre-existence and special designation of the Ahl al-Bayt. This linguistic derivation serves as a theological marker for the continuity of prophethood and imamate within the Prophet's household.

en.basel-kadem: 8.	We were told by Hussain bin Muhammed bin Yahya al-Alawi, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: I was told by my grandfather, that he said: I was told by Ahmad bin Saleh al-Tamimi, that he said: We were told by Abdullah bin Isa, from Ja’far bin Muhammed, from his father, peace be upon them both, that he said:

Jibra’eel, peace be upon him, gifted to the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, the name of Hasan bin Ali in a cloth of silk from the clothes of Paradise, and he derived the name of Hussain from Hasan, peace be upon them both.
